sections.admission_summary: Chief complaint: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, polyuria, altered consciousness. Admitted for inpatient care.
sections.discharge_diagnoses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia (E11.65). Secondary diagnoses: aspiration pneumonia, DVT.
sections.discharge_instructions: Drink plenty of fluids. Get adequate rest and avoid overexertion. Follow up with PCP in 7-10 days. Complete prescribed medications as directed. Return to ER if symptoms worsen. Follow diabetic diet plan; maintain hydration especially during illness (small sips frequently). Check blood glucose 4-6 times daily; check urine or blood ketones if BG >250 mg/dL. Return to ER for BG >300 mg/dL with ketones, persistent vomiting, deep breathing, or altered mental status. Gradual return to normal activity. Maintain a balanced diet.
sections.follow_up: Follow up with PCP in 7-10 days.
sections.hospital_course: Length of stay: 3 days (primary reason: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, polyuria, altered consciousness). Main treatment: anticoagulation (Enoxaparin); insulin (Insulin, Regular, Human); other parenteral drugs (Potassium Chloride). Key procedures: Central venous catheter insertion (2024-06-15). Complications during stay: aspiration pneumonia (onset hospital day 3), DVT (onset hospital day 3). Significant results: glucose 551 mg/dL [critical] (prior 578) on hospital day 1, treated with Insulin, Regular, Human; pH 7.04 [critical] on hospital day 1. Medication changes from admission: started Insulin Glargine. Condition at discharge: discharged home, Barthel Index 80/100.

sections.adl_assessment: Barthel Index 80/100 → minimal assistance (Feeding 10, Bathing 5, Mobility 10, Toilet use 5)
sections.care_plan: Care plan: hourly I/O, coordinate IV rate titration with MD; q1-2h glucose + serum K monitoring, early hypoglycemia / hypokalemia recognition; continuous mental-status + Kussmaul-respiration assessment; infection source workup (urine / LRT) + temperature trending.
sections.nursing_diagnosis: Nursing diagnoses: deficient fluid volume, risk for electrolyte imbalance, unstable glycemic control, risk for infection.
